options.text: The percentage of reactant atoms that are converted into the desired product
The number of atoms in a molecule
The cost of the atoms used in a reaction
The speed at which atoms react

questions.explanation: Atom economy measures the proportion of reactant atoms that end up in the desired (useful) product. A high atom economy means less waste is produced.

questions.stem: What is the formula for atom economy?

options.text: Atom economy = (Mr of all products / Mr of desired product) x 100
Atom economy = (Mr of desired product / sum of Mr of all reactants) x 100
Atom economy = (actual yield / theoretical yield) x 100
Atom economy = (mass of reactants / mass of products) x 100

questions.explanation: Atom economy = (Mr of desired product / sum of Mr of all reactants) x 100. This tells you what fraction of the total reactant mass becomes the useful product.

questions.stem: Which type of reaction always has 100% atom economy?

options.text: Decomposition reactions
Addition reactions (where only one product is formed)
Displacement reactions
Neutralisation reactions

questions.explanation: Addition reactions have 100% atom economy because all the reactant atoms end up in a single product. No atoms are wasted in by-products.

questions.stem: Why is a high atom economy desirable in industrial processes?

options.text: It makes the reaction go faster
It reduces waste and is more sustainable
It increases the temperature of the reaction
It means no catalyst is needed

questions.explanation: High atom economy means more reactant atoms are converted into useful product and fewer end up as waste by-products. This is better for the environment and more cost-effective.

questions.stem: How does atom economy differ from percentage yield?

options.text: They are the same thing
Atom economy is about the efficiency of the equation; percentage yield is about how much product is actually obtained
Percentage yield is always higher than atom economy
Atom economy measures temperature changes; percentage yield measures mass changes

questions.explanation: Atom economy measures the theoretical efficiency of a reaction based on the equation (how much of the reactants can become the desired product). Percentage yield measures the practical efficiency (how much product was actually obtained).

questions.stem: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂. What is the atom economy for producing CaO? [Mr: CaCO₃ = 100, CaO = 56, CO₂ = 44]
questions.explanation: Atom economy = (Mr of desired product / Mr of reactants) x 100 = (56/100) x 100 = 56%. The remaining 44% of the mass becomes CO₂ (a by-product).

questions.stem: A reaction produces a desired product and two by-products. What can you say about its atom economy?

options.text: It will be 100%
It will be less than 100% because some atoms end up in the by-products
It cannot be calculated
It depends on the temperature

questions.explanation: If by-products are formed, then some of the reactant atoms are being used to make these unwanted products instead of the desired one. This means the atom economy will be less than 100%.
